description: AD ASTRA is a team focused on programming, geospatial data analysis, and space exploration. We turn Earth and space data into practical insights, using code to build tools that help us understand our planet and explore what lies beyond it.
summary: Raíces Profundas (Deep Roots) is a bilingual (ES/EN) trend-detective app for the Central American Dry Corridor, where recurrent drought and heat threaten millions of smallholder farmers. Users choose what to investigate (root-zone soil moisture from NASA SMAP L4, or precipitation, air temperature, maximum temperature, soil wetness, humidity and evapotranspiration from NASA MERRA-2 via NASA POWER), where (25 ~1° cells labelled by nearest town, coordinates and landscape type, or a click on the map) and when (whole year, Primera, canícula, Postrera or dry season, any period 1981–2025). The app answers four questions in a "detective's verdict" — what is changing, where, how much and whether it is statistically significant — using Sen's slope with a 95% confidence interval, the Mann–Kendall test, linear regression with a t-test and 95% CI, and a seasonal Mann–Kendall test on monthly anomalies. A trend map highlights cells with significant change, so users can see that the same variable can trend in opposite directions in different regions (e.g. maximum temperature warming in the western highlands while cooling in eastern Honduras).
details:
• Variables: SMAP L4 sm_rootzone (SPL4SMGP v008, 2015–2025); MERRA-2 PRECTOTCORR, T2M, T2M_MAX, GWETROOT, GWETTOP, RH2M, EVLAND (monthly, 1981–2025).
  • Pipeline: FAO Dry Corridor boundary → ~1° grid → SMAP subset with NASA Harmony/earthaccess and averaged per cell and season; MERRA-2 monthly series from the NASA POWER API at a representative point per cell.
  • Statistics: seasonal means per year → Sen's slope (+95% CI), Mann–Kendall τ and p, OLS slope, t-test p, R², 95% CI; seasonal Mann–Kendall on anomalies with the seasonal cycle removed.
  • Learning aids: three solved cases (2023 El Niño drought, highland warming, opposite regional trends), topic-based variable suggestions by landscape, plain-language glossary, CSV downloads and links to Giovanni, AppEEARS, Data Rods, NASA POWER and KNMI Climate Explorer.
  • Exploratory extra: a clearly-labelled linear extrapolation of SMAP soil moisture to 2030.
  • Tools: Python, pandas, GeoPandas, SciPy, Streamlit, Plotly, earthaccess, NASA Harmony, Render.
  • URL for repository : https://github.com/w2k31984/dry-corridor-roots-earth.git
